# A7 Scope and Sequence, 2026–27 — the backbone on the calendar

**Status:** proposed 20 September 2026 for Croix's approval. Generated by `tools/scope_calendar.py`;
edit the PLAN there and re-run — the day table below is never hand-edited.
**Companions:** `B1G-M BACKBONE.md` (what each benchmark requires), `MATH NATION A7 BOOK - table of
contents and IXL plan.md` (the book's order and IXL's skills), `SCOPE AND SEQUENCE 2026-2027.md`
(the county's sheet, kept for its "essential" flags only).

## The four decisions this plan is built on (Croix, 20 Sept)

1. **Book order stands.** Units 3 → 17 in Math Nation's order, because that is the commitment made
   with his dad and where admin expects the class to be. Students never open the book; the order is
   the visible thing.
2. **Three woven threads** bring the Q4 Grade 8 benchmarks forward *without* moving a unit. Each
   thread is two periods dropped into the unit that already teaches the same idea with numbers:
   - **Thread A** (in Unit 3): the exponent laws with variable bases — 8.AR.1.1. Same laws, same
     week, x instead of 5. Unit 14 later becomes a one-day consolidation plus the two things that
     are genuinely new there (monomial × linear, factoring).
   - **Thread B** (in Unit 6): angle pairs and the triangle angle theorems — 8.GR.1.4, 8.GR.1.5.
     The Triangle Sum Theorem is on the FAST reference sheet next to the Triangle Inequality
     Theorem the unit already teaches. Unit 16 later is one consolidation day plus polygons.
   - **Thread C** (in Unit 13): sample spaces and theoretical probability of repeated experiments —
     8.DP.2.1, 8.DP.2.2 — taught beside the data unit. Unit 17 later is two days plus predictions.
   Admin sees Unit 3, Unit 6, Unit 13 on the board. FAST sees every Grade 8 benchmark taught before
   PM2 except transformations, polygons and predictions, all scheduled by mid-April.
3. **Compression:** the book's paired lessons run as one period (`4.02+03` means lessons 4.2 and
   4.3 in one period), and the Grade-7-only units — circles/circle graphs (8), cylinders (9), data
   displays (13.1–13.3) — run short. Nothing is skipped; the carried Grade 7 benchmarks are all
   taught, just not at the book's length. They are not on the Grade 8 FAST.
4. **Assessment:** every unit exam is two periods (Croix's practice); quizzes live inside periods and
   take the warm-up. Units 8–9 and 15–16 share an exam; Unit 17's is one period.

Plus one flex day after each Q1–Q3 exam (except Unit 5 and Unit 7): reteach from what the exam
showed, or absorb a lost day. Q4 has no flex days because the PM3 review block is the buffer.

## How a thread period works (so it does not become a "bonus" lesson)

A thread period is a normal period: slides → whiteboards → IXL, 53 minutes, one lesson plan, one
TE, its own whiteboard round with named distractors. It is named on the slide by its own title
("Exponent laws with variable bases"), not as "Unit 14 preview." In the unit exam that follows,
the thread's benchmark gets one or two questions like any other lesson in the unit. When the book
reaches the consolidation unit (14, 16, 17), the first period is a retrieval day built from the
thread's own question bank, and only the genuinely new content gets full lessons.

## IXL for the last five minutes

Each lesson row in the book table names IXL's aligned skill(s); those are the day's posted skills.
Thread periods use the consolidation unit's skills (14.1–14.4, 16.1–16.2, 17.1–17.2). Eleven book
lessons have no IXL skill; on those days the neighbouring lesson's skill stays posted.
